The densest connected graph on \(2n\) vertices in which a single cop cannot guarantee capture (so Alice can evade forever) is obtained by taking the complete graph \(K_{2n}\) and deleting a perfect matching.  
Each vertex then misses exactly one neighbour, giving every closed neighbourhood a unique missing vertex; consequently no vertex’s closed neighbourhood is contained in another’s, so the graph is not dismantlable and has cop‑number ≥ 2.  

The complete graph on \(2n\) vertices has \(\frac{2n(2n-1)}{2}=n(2n-1)\) edges. Removing a perfect matching deletes exactly \(n\) edges, leaving  

\[
n(2n-1)-n = n(2n-2)=2n(n-1)
\]

edges.

Thus the maximum possible number of edges is  

**ANSWER: \(2n(n-1)\)**
